architecture.purpose: The Electron main process is the orchestration core of TallyBridge: it boots the app, applies one-time config migrations, spawns the bundled Python sync engine as short-lived subprocesses, runs a loopback HTTP server on port 3002 for cloud-initiated voucher pushes, polls the cloud control plane for queued pushes, and bridges a curated IPC surface to the React renderer. It also manages the system tray, electron-store config, auto-update, and a BetterStack remote-log forwarder, while guarding single-threaded TallyPrime (port 9000) from concurrent/heavy reads.

entrypoints.role: App bootstrap: initLogger (prod only), runs two one-time store migrations, creates the BrowserWindow, instantiates SyncEngine/LocalPushServer/PushQueuePoller, wires tray + IPC + auto-updater, schedules first sync after 8s, handles before-quit/window-all-closed lifecycle
contextBridge sandbox boundary: exposes window.electronAPI (invoke wrappers + an allow-listed event on/off) to the renderer with contextIsolation:true, nodeIntegration:false
Registers all ipcMain.handle channels; also the in-process Tally XML client (axios POST to port 9000) used for company discovery, capability probing, and date-range reads

keyModules.responsibility: Sync orchestration (Tally->Cloud). Port 9000 pre-flight via raw TCP socket; spawns Python sync_main.py / tallybridge-engine.exe per company; run-tracking with runId/cancelledRunIds; pause kills child via taskkill /f /t (win32) or SIGKILL; idle (10min) + hard (45min) timeouts; parses last JSON stdout line for record counts; interval scheduling (default 360min)

IPC surface + Tally XML/ODBC integration: get-config, save-settings, add/remove-company, sync-now, pause/resume-sync, check-tally(-capabilities), get-tally-companies, get-tally-company-date-ranges, startup-setting, open-log-file. Includes XML envelope builders, UTF-16/entity decoding, ODBC probe via SysWOW64 powershell helper

HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:3002 (Cloud->Tally). Loopback-only guard, 1MB body cap, routes GET /health and POST /push-voucher; spawns Python push worker (TB_COMMAND=push_voucher) feeding payload over stdin; EADDRINUSE shows a dialog
Polls the control plane every 5s (TB_COMMAND=poll_push_queue) per enabled company; spawns Python per company; skips when paused or a sync is in progress; filters noisy 'no pending' log lines

electron-store schema (tallybridge-config) + defaults; Company/AppConfig types; add/remove/updateCompanyStatus; resetStaleSyncStatuses; normalizers and resolveControlPlane*/resolveSyncIngest* fallback helpers (controlPlaneUrl||backendUrl legacy)

electron-updater wiring: autoDownload, hourly + initial checkForUpdates, installWhenIdle defers quitAndInstall until isBusy()==false, beforeInstall() tears down servers; download-update/install-update IPC

BetterStack/Logtail forwarder: taps sync-log lines, batches (flush 2s / 50 lines / 1000 cap), POSTs over https; baked-in token+host with env overrides; fully try/catch wrapped so it never throws into sync; setLogContext tags lines with active company identity
System tray icon + context menu (Open / Sync Now / Quit via app.exit(0)); setStatus(idle|syncing|error|paused) rebuilds the menu and tooltip
File logger to app logs dir (tallybridge.log) with 5MB rotation to .old.log; monkeypatches console.log/warn/error in production; never throws on write failure

risks: Single-threaded Tally (port 9000) contention: although runAllCompanies/poller guard against overlap via isSyncInProgress, the in-process axios Tally calls in ipc-handlers (check-tally, get-tally-companies, add-company, date-ranges) are NOT coordinated with the sync engine — a user clicking Refresh/Add Company during a sync can fire a concurrent read into the single-engine gateway and contribute to the documented freeze

Idle/hard timeout kill uses proc.kill() (SIGTERM equivalent) at sync-engine.ts:525/537, but pause uses taskkill /f /t. On Windows the bundled exe may spawn child processes; the timeout path does not use the /t tree-kill, so an orphaned engine subprocess could survive a timeout while currentProc is cleared on close

Port 3002 race / EADDRINUSE: only surfaced via a blocking dialog (local-push-server.ts:152-157); the server never retries or falls back, so a stale instance leaves push delivery dead until manual restart. localPushServer.stop() calls server.close() but does not await in-flight connections

Swallowed errors: remote-log flush/ship, logger write, and Python push-worker JSON parse failures are intentionally swallowed; JSON parse failure in sync finalize (sync-engine.ts:455) only console.errors and silently falls back to previous record counts, so a malformed Python result is reported as success with stale counts

Push queue poller spawns one Python process per enabled company every 5s; with many companies or a slow Python cold-start, polls can stack up wall-clock time even though scheduleNext only fires in finally — combined with per-company Tally reads this adds steady load on the Tally engine

Auto-updater installWhenIdle polls isBusy() every 5s indefinitely; if a sync run hangs (despite timeouts) the install can be deferred a long time. beforeInstall sets isQuitting and stops servers but does not kill an in-flight Python sync child before quitAndInstall

local-push-server pickCompanyName auto-selects the sole enabled company when company_name is absent; if cloud sends a push without company context and multiple companies exist it throws (400) — correct, but a single-company misconfiguration could route a push to the wrong company silently
techDebt: Python command resolution (dev 'py -3 -u' vs prod resourcesPath exe) is duplicated in three files: sync-engine.ts:300-307, local-push-server.ts:99-117, push-queue-poller.ts:21-39 — should be a shared helper

Legacy dual config keys (backendUrl/apiKey vs controlPlaneUrl/controlPlaneApiKey) persist; save-settings writes both and resolve* helpers fall back, adding ongoing branching that should be consolidated post-migration
spawn(...) return values for the pause taskkill (sync-engine.ts:116) and the timeout-driven kills are not error-handled; a spawn failure there is silent

Idle/hard timeout values are read from process.env at call time inside syncOneCompany rather than centralized config; magic numbers (8000ms first-sync defer, 60s Tally retry, 5s poll, 360min) are scattered as inline literals
remote-log baked-in production token+host in source is a maintenance/security smell even if write-only; rotating it requires a code change and release

architecture.purpose: The TallyBridge desktop UI: a Vite + React 19 SPA that runs in the Electron renderer process and is the control surface for the sync connector. It lets users add/remove TallyPrime companies, edit sync/connection/ingest settings, watch a live sync log, and manage in-app auto-updates. All real work (Tally reads, sync, config persistence) happens in the main process; the renderer only renders state and calls main over a context-isolated IPC bridge.

entrypoints.role: Vite HTML root (Vite root dir = src/renderer); mounts #root and loads main.tsx as a module; also holds the only real global CSS (a small <style> block: box reset, body font, input/button base, custom scrollbar)
React bootstrap: ReactDOM.createRoot(#root).render(<React.StrictMode><App/></React.StrictMode>)
Root component: HashRouter + route table; lays out UpdateBanner (top) / Sidebar + <main> / StatusBar (bottom) as a flex column
contextBridge that defines the window.electronAPI surface the whole renderer depends on (not under src/renderer but is the renderer's only door to main)
Ambient TS declaration of window.electronAPI; the renderer's compile-time contract for IPC (drifted from preload — see risks)

keyModules.responsibility: Routing + shell layout. HashRouter (chosen for file://-loaded Electron). Routes: / -> HomeGuided, /add-company -> AddCompanyGuided, /settings -> Settings, /log -> SyncLog, /about -> About, * -> redirect to /. Persistent chrome: UpdateBanner, Sidebar, StatusBar.

Main dashboard. Loads companies + syncPaused via getConfig(); renders CompanyCardStable list or EmptyState; Sync All / Pause-Resume / Add buttons. Subscribes to companies-updated, sync-start, sync-complete, sync-paused events to drive isSyncing/isPaused/company state.

The entire config surface. Local form state mirrors AppConfig; loads via getConfig()+getStartupSetting(); writes via saveSettings(form). Also fetches Tally company date ranges, tests connectivity/capabilities, toggles Windows startup, opens log file. Largest, most complex page.

Add-company wizard, a 6-state machine (loading/select/noTally/checking/success/error). Lists companies open in Tally via getTallyCompanies(), commits via addCompany(selection). Has explicit loading/empty/error UX (best in the app).

Live terminal-style log. Subscribes to sync-log IPC events, keeps a rolling buffer (slice(-500)) of {time,company,line,isError}, auto-scrolls to bottom, Clear button. Heuristic error coloring via substring match on 'error'/'[err'.
Static about panel; reads version via getAppVersion(). Contains placeholder support email 'support@yourcompany.com'.
Left nav with NavLink active styling; shows app version (getAppVersion). Nav list is hardcoded (Home/Sync Log/Settings/About) — note it omits Add Company (reached only via Home buttons).

Bottom bar: Tally connectivity (polls checkTally every 10s), pause state, and a next-sync countdown timer derived from syncIntervalMinutes. Internet status is hardcoded true (const [internetOk]=useState(true)).

Auto-update banner state machine (available/downloading/downloaded/installing/error) driven by update-* IPC events; user-controlled downloadUpdate()/installUpdate(); dismissible. Suppresses background-check errors unless user is mid download/install.
The ACTIVE company card (used by HomeGuided). Renders name, identity hint (formalName/GUID), status dot, last-sync record counts, error text, and a confirm()-gated Remove button.
Ambient window.electronAPI type. Declares config/company/sync/update methods + on/off. Source of compile-time IPC typing.

externalInterfaces.target: Electron main process via preload contextBridge (window.electronAPI)
externalInterfaces.protocol: Electron IPC (ipcRenderer.invoke for request/response; ipcRenderer.on for push events)
externalInterfaces.notes: The ONLY external interface. invoke channels: get-config, save-settings, get-app-version, add-company, remove-company, get-companies, sync-now, pause-sync, resume-sync, check-tally, check-tally-capabilities, get-tally-companies, get-tally-company-date-ranges, get-startup-setting, set-startup-setting, open-log-file, download-update, install-update. Push event channels (allowlisted in preload ALLOWED_CHANNELS): sync-log, sync-start, sync-complete, sync-paused, companies-updated, update-available, update-progress, update-downloaded, update-error, plus company-status-change/company-synced/company-error (allowlisted but no renderer subscriber found).

Renderer never talks to Tally (port 9000), the Express backend (3001), the local push server (3002), or Supabase directly. All such access is mediated by the main process; the renderer is purely a presentation/IPC client. Good security posture (contextIsolation, channel allowlist).

Edit settings: Settings mounts -> Promise.all(getConfig(), getStartupSetting()) hydrates a local SettingsForm + startup toggle -> loadCompanyDateRanges() calls getTallyCompanyDateRanges() to populate from/to date pickers -> Save invokes saveSettings(form) which persists the whole form object to electron-store; a 2s 'Settings Saved!' confirmation then resets.

Manual sync: HomeGuided handleSyncNow() optimistically sets isSyncing then invokes syncNow(); main emits sync-start/sync-complete and per-company companies-updated; StatusBar resets its countdown on sync-complete; CompanyCardStable shows per-company status/record counts.

Pause/resume: HomeGuided handlePauseResume() invokes pauseSync()/resumeSync(); main broadcasts sync-paused which both HomeGuided and StatusBar consume to update pause UI and freeze the countdown to '--:--'.
Live log: main streams sync-log events -> SyncLog appends to a rolling 500-line buffer and auto-scrolls; Clear empties local state (does not clear main-side logs/file).

Auto-update: main emits update-available/progress/downloaded/error -> UpdateBanner advances its phase; user clicks drive downloadUpdate()/installUpdate(); installUpdate() returns {deferred} so banner can say 'will install once current sync finishes'.
Connectivity telemetry: StatusBar polls checkTally() every 10s for the Tally dot; Settings 'Test'/'Check Capabilities' buttons call checkTally()/checkTallyCapabilities() on demand.
configAndSecrets: No env vars or secrets are read in the renderer itself (no import.meta.env usage in src/renderer). VITE_BACKEND_URL exists at the project level but is consumed by main, not these files.

Settings.tsx is the config-WRITE surface; saveSettings(form) persists these AppConfig keys to electron-store (main/store.ts): tallyUrl, syncIntervalMinutes, controlPlaneUrl(+legacy backendUrl read fallback), controlPlaneApiKey(+legacy apiKey fallback), syncIngestMode (render|hybrid|direct), syncIngestUrl, syncIngestKey, syncContractVersion, accountEmail, readMode (auto|xml-only|hybrid), odbcDsnOverride, syncFromDate, syncToDate.

Secret-ish inputs rendered as type=password: controlPlaneApiKey (Settings.tsx:427) and syncIngestKey (Settings.tsx:466). These are typed/saved in plaintext through IPC into electron-store; the renderer offers no masking-on-display beyond the password input and no validation.
syncPaused and companies[] are read (getConfig) but written via dedicated IPC (pause/resume, add/remove), not via saveSettings.
Windows 'Start on login' is config-adjacent but routed through get/set-startup-setting IPC (likely app.setLoginItemSettings in main), not the form.
risks: IPC type-contract drift: Settings.tsx calls window.electronAPI.getStartupSetting (160), setStartupSetting (494), and openLogFile (504), but NONE are declared in electron.d.ts (lines 19-41). They exist in preload.ts, so runtime works, but TypeScript typing is a lie — any signature change to these channels won't be caught at compile time. The .d.ts is hand-maintained and already out of sync.

readMode option mismatch: store.ts AppConfig.readMode allows auto|xml-only|hybrid but CLAUDE.md/MEMORY reference a 'shadow' mode; Settings only exposes 3 of them. If a config carries readMode:'shadow' it cannot be re-selected via the dropdown (silently shows blank/first).

StatusBar countdown is cosmetic and lies: it is a pure client-side setInterval seeded from syncIntervalMinutes (StatusBar.tsx:43), not from main's real next-sync schedule. It only resets on sync-complete and on mount, so after the app sits idle or sync timing shifts, 'Next in X' will not reflect the actual scheduler.

Internet status is hardcoded: const [internetOk]=useState(true) with no setter (StatusBar.tsx:5) — the 'Internet: OK' dot is always green and never reflects real connectivity, which is misleading during cloud-push failures.

Undefined CSS animation: all three CompanyCard variants set animation:'pulse 1s infinite' for the syncing state, but no @keyframes pulse is defined anywhere in src/renderer or index.html — the syncing pulse silently no-ops (verified via grep).

SyncLog error detection is a fragile substring heuristic (line.includes('error')||'[err'); benign lines containing 'error' are mis-colored red and structured severity from Python is lost. Log buffer is renderer-only and lost on navigation away/remount (state not lifted), and Clear doesn't touch the persisted log file.

Settings.handleSave has no error handling: if saveSettings rejects, the UI still flashes 'Settings Saved!' (no try/catch around the await at line 201), giving false success feedback. Same optimistic pattern in HomeGuided (sets isSyncing before/without checking syncNow result).
About.tsx ships a placeholder support contact 'support@yourcompany.com' (line 21) — a production polish gap visible to end users.
techDebt: Guided vs non-guided duplication is largely DEAD CODE, not real duplication: Home.tsx and AddCompany.tsx are one-line re-exports of their *Guided siblings with the old implementation left commented out below (Home.tsx:1-2 + commented block, AddCompany.tsx:1 + commented block). The commented-out originals still contain bugs (e.g. AddCompany uses an undefined setSelected/selected) and should be deleted rather than kept as 'documentation'.

State management is intentionally minimal (per-component useState + direct IPC), which is fine for this size, but there is no shared store/context — companies and config are independently re-fetched in HomeGuided, Settings, and StatusBar, and pause/interval state is duplicated across HomeGuided and StatusBar with separate event subscriptions.

Accessibility gaps: icons are decorative glyph strings (⊞/≡/⚙) and emoji-substitute placeholders ('[]','OK','X','...') in the *Guided pages with no aria-labels; company-select rows are clickable <div>s (AddCompanyGuided.tsx:121) with no role/keyboard handling; uses native confirm()/window.alert-style confirm for Remove. The Settings 'Field' helper associates label-for only for the startup checkbox (htmlFor='startOnLogin'), most other inputs lack id/for association.

architecture.purpose: The Python sync engine is a single-shot subprocess spawned by the Electron main process (sync-engine.ts) that bridges a local TallyPrime/Tally.ERP 9 instance with the cloud. It reads masters/vouchers/reports from Tally's XML-RPC server on port 9000 (with an optional Tally ODBC fast-path), batches and uploads them to the cloud either via the Express control-plane (/api/sync) or directly to Supabase PostgREST RPCs, and on a separate invocation pushes Sales/Purchase vouchers back into Tally via XML Import. All behavior is driven by environment variables passed at spawn time; output is line-buffered stdout plus a final JSON result line.

entrypoints.role: main() — process entry; dispatches on TB_COMMAND to sync (default), push_voucher (single direct push from stdin), or poll_push_queue; returns 0/1 exit code
Thin alias entrypoint: `from sync_main import main; sys.exit(main())` — the PyInstaller bundle target (tallybridge-engine.exe)
Electron-side spawner: selects tallybridge-engine.exe (prod) or sync_main.py (dev), builds the env block (lines 371-394), enforces idle/hard timeouts (lines 403-409)
run_single_push_command() — reads one voucher JSON from stdin, calls tally_pusher.push_vouchers, prints JSON result (TB_COMMAND=push_voucher)
run_poll_push_queue_command() — polls backend push queue and imports pending vouchers quietly (TB_COMMAND=poll_push_queue)

keyModules.responsibility: Orchestration brain: read-mode/ingest-mode decisioning, FY-date resolution & clamping, change detection vs cached alter IDs, per-section fetch with ODBC->XML fallback, month/window voucher batching with recursive split-on-timeout, payload assembly, heartbeat thread, push-cycle dispatch

Upload layer: push() routes by SYNC_INGEST_MODE (render -> POST /api/sync; hybrid/direct -> Supabase PostgREST RPCs tb_ingest_phase3_hybrid + chunked tb_ingest_vouchers); company resolve/upsert; backend alter-id lookup, push-queue fetch, push-results post; ReadTimeout post-verify polling

Tally XML-RPC transport on port 9000: requests.Session, UTF-8/UTF-16 request encode + response decode, connect/read timeouts, STATUS/LINEERROR checks, detect_tally_product(), and all hand-written TDL export envelopes (company info, alter IDs, groups, ledgers, vouchers, stock, outstanding, P&L/BS/TB)

Push (Cloud->Tally): validates/normalizes a Sales/Purchase voucher, derives signed amounts and party/inventory ledger matching, renders a Tally Import VOUCHER envelope, POSTs it, and parses CREATED/ALTERED/ERRORS/LINEERROR from the response

Definition-driven (JSON-config) collection requests and response parsing via xmltodict; builds COLLECTION/Data envelopes from definitions/structured_sections.json and finalizes per-section row shapes (vouchers/P&L/BS/TB) incl. stock part_code mailing-name unwrap

Optional Tally ODBC fast-path: drives a long-lived PowerShell helper (tally_odbc_helper.ps1) over stdin/stdout JSON to probe/query DSNs for groups/ledgers/stock; normalizes rows via definitions/odbc_sections.json; provides XML-vs-ODBC shadow comparison

Legacy fallback parsers (xmltodict) for all sections plus shared helpers: clean_xml (strips control chars), safe_float/int/str (dict-aware), parse_tally_date, parse_alter_ids, parse_vouchers, parse_voucher_headers
Standalone dev MITM proxy (port 9001 -> 9000) to capture/print BizAnalyst<->Tally XML; not part of the sync runtime
Standalone dev tool: fires 10 hardcoded Export reports at port 9000 and saves raw XML to tally-responses/ for inspection; hardcodes COMPANY='Demo Trading Co'

risks: Single-threaded Tally-9000 hang (documented in memory): port 9000 shares one engine with the interactive UI, so heavy/full-FY voucher pulls and stock valuation freeze TallyPrime. Mitigations are window batching (7-day default) + recursive split-on-timeout + pacing knob, but a single non-splittable window that times out still raises and a full-FY catch-up on a stale cache can lock the client (the 1.2.11 freeze RCA).

TallyPrime voucher-XML safety was REVERTED (sync_main.py CHANGE 1/2/4): should_skip_voucher_family now always returns False and Day Book fallback is enabled for TallyPrime, so voucher exports run on TallyPrime again — exactly the path previously disabled to avoid the port-9000 crash. This is on the experimental branch and reintroduces freeze/crash exposure.

Day Book fallback can corrupt voucher identity/dates: fetch_day_book_voucher_window admits a best-effort result when no request shape honors the requested window, and validate_voucher_batch only WARNS (does not reject) when a Day Book export collapses to a single date — risking wrong-dated vouchers being ingested.

ReadTimeout 'post-verify' in render mode (verify_remote_sync_completion) treats an upload as successful purely from matching remote alter IDs + a newer last_synced_at, which can mark a partial/failed ingest as done if the backend updated markers before fully persisting.

Direct-ingest company resolution races: _DIRECT_COMPANY_ID is process-cached and resolution falls back to match by name when GUID is absent; a name with no GUID can bind to the wrong company, and the insert path assumes companies.name uniqueness. Each sync run resets the cache (push() sets _DIRECT_COMPANY_ID=None).

Backend error swallowing: _check_response/_extract_backend_error and several try/except blocks downgrade failures to warnings and continue; voucher-family errors silently zero out vouchers/outstanding/reports for the run while still reporting success (alter-ID cache is correctly NOT updated then), so masters can advance while vouchers silently lag.

ODBC helper fragility: spawns powershell.exe per DSN candidate over a single stdin/stdout line protocol; a hung helper or partial readline raises and only falls back to XML — no independent timeout on the readline beyond the helper-reported timeout.

Regex-based XML parsing in tally_client._check_response and tally_pusher.parse_push_response (CREATED/ALTERED/LINEERROR via re.findall) is brittle against XML structure/encoding variation and could miscount import errors.
techDebt: sync_main.py is 1905 LOC with a deeply nested main(); the voucher path carries explicit 'CHANGE 1-4' revert markers (header comment lines 1-20) indicating an in-flight experimental branch state rather than a settled design.

Three parallel parsing systems coexist: definition-driven (definition_extractor + structured_sections.json), legacy hand-written parsers (xml_parser), and ODBC normalization (odbc_sections.json) — every section has a try-structured/except-legacy ladder duplicated inline.

Hand-built XML string templates throughout tally_client.py and tally_pusher.py (f-strings) rather than a builder; push voucher XML embeds many hardcoded GST-invoice-shape constants (REQUESTORRULE, SERIALMASTER, batch INDENTNO/ORDERNO placeholders).

Duplicated config parsing: SYNC_INGEST_MODE/URL/CONTRACT_VERSION are independently re-read and re-validated in both sync_main.py and cloud_pusher.py.
Two legacy env aliases (BACKEND_URL/API_KEY vs CONTROL_PLANE_URL/CONTROL_PLANE_API_KEY) are both honored, and sync-engine.ts sets all four to the same values — redundant.

Incremental voucher sync exists (ENABLE_INCREMENTAL_VOUCHER_SYNC, 7-day overlap) but main() hardcodes a full sync_plan before change detection and only narrows via build_sync_plan; its value is undercut by full-FY windows on first/forced syncs.

architecture.component: Express Cloud Backend (TallyBridge API, port 3001, GCP Cloud Run)
architecture.purpose: A thin, stateless Express 5 (ESM/TypeScript) cloud API that ingests TallyPrime/ERP data from the desktop connector and serves it to the Flutter app and web dashboard, backed by Supabase (Postgres) and GCS. It is the central node of the multi-tenant model (one Supabase project per client), authenticating callers via Firebase JWT or a shared API key and exposing one giant /api/sync ingest endpoint plus read endpoints, a cloud->Tally push queue, and an inventory-intelligence ("reorder-levels") report computed in-process.

2992-line core router: POST /api/sync ingest + push-queue lifecycle + all dashboard GET reads + reorder-levels inventory report
POST /api/push-voucher and GET /api/push-voucher/health: reverse-proxies a voucher JSON to the desktop local-push-server (default http://127.0.0.1:3002)
POST /api/push-invoice: builds a hardcoded GST-SALE voucher (9% CGST + 9% SGST) from {party_name, items} and forwards to the local push server
requireApiKey: Firebase Bearer JWT verify, else timingSafeEqual on x-api-key vs API_KEY

keyModules.responsibility: Everything: auth wiring, payload normalization/validation, company upsert + GUID/name resolution, voucher graph ingest with snapshot/rollback, snapshot-section replacement (outstanding/PnL/BS/TB), push_queue enqueue/activate/poll/results, GCS invoice-image proxy, dashboard GET reads, and the in-memory inventory scenario classifier + reorder-levels report (JSON/CSV)
Dual auth: Firebase ID-token verification (Flutter users) with API-key fallback compared via constant-time timingSafeEqual; 401 on length mismatch or failure
Single shared Supabase service-role client from SUPABASE_URL + SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY (non-null-asserted; bypasses RLS)
firebase-admin init from base64 service-account JSON (FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_B64); throws at import time if unset
GCS client (ADC on Cloud Run) for scanned invoice page JPEGs under {rowId}/page-{n}.jpg; best-effort uploads, exists check, read stream; disabled (no-op) when INVOICE_BUCKET unset

dataFlows: Sync ingest (Tally->Cloud): Python cloud_pusher POSTs /api/sync with {company_name, company_guid, company_info, alter_ids, groups, ledgers, vouchers, stock_items, outstanding, profit_loss, balance_sheet, trial_balance, sync_meta} -> requireApiKey -> validate each section is array <=100k rows -> upsertCompanyRecord (resolve by guid, then by unique name, then insert) -> upsert groups/ledgers/stock_items on (company_id,name) -> voucher graph: snapshot existing rows, upsert vouchers on (company_id,tally_guid), insert voucher_items + voucher_ledger_entries returning ids, delete old child rows, derive purchases for purchase-type vouchers, reconcile (delete stale guids per voucher_sync_mode full/incremental) -> insert-then-cleanup snapshot sections (outstanding/PnL/BS/TB) gated by per-section last_*_synced_at timestamp -> update companies sync-state -> best-effort sync_log insert (falls back without sync_meta column) -> 200 {success, company_id, records}

Ingest failure path: on any throw before company sync-state is persisted, restore the voucher-graph snapshot and roll back inserted snapshot-section rows; errors with schema-cache/relation/column text get 'apply backend/full_schema.sql' guidance appended; 500 returned

Push enqueue (parsing->cloud): parsing service POSTs /api/sync/push-queue with nested {push_queue_payload|tally_payload|...} + optional scanned_images_b64 -> resolveCompanyLookup (no successful-sync required) -> normalizePushVoucherPayload (strict type/date/party/ledger/item validation, relaxed for alien OCR vouchers) -> insert push_queue row (status 'pending') -> best-effort upload page JPEGs to GCS under row id, store {scan:{pages}} on source_payload

Push activation/poll/results: app POSTs /push-queue/activate (pending->push_now, optional company ownership check) -> desktop push-queue-poller GETs /push-queue?company_*&limit (returns push_now jobs, type-filtered) -> poller pushes to Tally -> POSTs /push-results [{id,status:pushed|failed,error_message,tally_response}] which targeted-updates push_queue rows (no company scoping on the update)

Reorder-levels report: client GETs /api/sync/reorder-levels[/:reportKey]?company_*&threshold&limit&format -> requireClientApiKey (x-api-key vs API_KEY_CLIENT) -> resolveCompanyLookup on reorderSupabase -> fetchAllPages over GST SALE (6m) + purchase (1m) vouchers + voucher_items + stock_items -> classifyInventoryScenarioV2 in paise -> 15-scenario classification -> JSON or CSV download

Dashboard reads: app/web GET /vouchers,/outstanding,/stock,/purchases,/pnl,/balance-sheet,/trial-balance,/parties,/party-ledger,/alter-ids -> requireApiKey -> resolveCompanyLookup (most require last_synced_at) -> fetchAllPages (1000-row pagination) filtered by company_id and, for snapshot tables, the latest synced_at
Cloud->Tally direct push: app POSTs /api/push-voucher or /api/push-invoice -> requireApiKey -> reverse-proxy to TALLYBRIDGE_LOCAL_PUSH_URL (desktop:3002) -> TallyPrime; response (or 502) relayed back
configAndSecrets: SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY — shared service-role client (db/supabase.ts), non-null-asserted at import; service key BYPASSES RLS

SUPABASE_URL_Client (note mixed-case 'Url_Client' / SUPABASE_URL_Client), SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY_CLIENT — separate reorder-levels Supabase project (sync.ts:19-25); env name is case-sensitive per comment
API_KEY — service-to-service secret for requireApiKey, compared with timingSafeEqual (auth.ts:28-38)
API_KEY_CLIENT — separate secret for /reorder-levels (requireClientApiKey, sync.ts:31)
FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_B64 — base64 service-account JSON; db/firebase.ts THROWS at import if unset (hard startup failure)
INVOICE_BUCKET — GCS bucket for scanned pages; unset => image storage disabled (db/gcs.ts:8,11)
PORT (default 3001); TB_JSON_BODY_LIMIT (default 100mb, index.ts:10-13)
TALLYBRIDGE_LOCAL_PUSH_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3002/push-voucher), TALLYBRIDGE_LOCAL_HEALTH_URL (default :3002/health) — push proxies
TB_PUSH_ALLOWED_TYPES — CSV override of allowed push voucher types (default Sales,Purchase,GST SALE,GST PURCHASE; sync.ts:114-121)
GCS uses Application Default Credentials (Cloud Run compute SA) — no key file
No tb_ingest_masters RPC and no .rpc() call exist in this backend; the direct-write RPC path (per project memory) lives in the Python engine, not here
risks: Multi-tenancy depends entirely on per-client Supabase project + manual company_id WHERE filters; the service-role key bypasses RLS, so any cross-company query bug or a shared project leaks all tenants' data. RLS policies in SQL are permissive 'USING(true)' — they provide no isolation by design.

/push-results (sync.ts:2513) updates push_queue rows by id with NO company scoping and NO ownership check — any holder of API_KEY can mark any company's queued voucher pushed/failed and inject arbitrary tally_response JSON.
/push-queue/activate accepts company identity only optionally; when omitted (hasCompanyIdentity false) it activates a job by id with no tenant check (sync.ts:2400-2417).

The /api/sync ingest is NOT a real DB transaction — it is a hand-rolled snapshot+rollback across many separate PostgREST calls. A crash/timeout (Cloud Run request limit, OOM on 100mb body) between steps can leave vouchers/items/entries/purchases partially written and snapshot sections half-replaced; restore is best-effort and itself only console.error's on failure (restoreVoucherGraphSnapshot, restoreRows).

Inventory report and several reads pull ALL vouchers + voucher_items into memory via fetchAllPages (unbounded by 1000-row pages) and classify in JS; for large companies this is high-memory/CPU and can OOM the Cloud Run instance (echoes the prior render-mode 413/OOM history).
cors() is fully open (no origin allowlist) and there is no rate limiting; combined with a single shared API_KEY this is a broad attack surface.

express.json limit 100mb + base64 scanned images in the same JSON body means a single push can be very large; Cloud Run 32MB request cap (HTTP/1) can silently reject before the 100mb limit ever applies.

resolveCompanyLookup name-path returns 409 on duplicate names but the ingest upsertCompanyRecord can still create a second same-name company if guid differs, then later name lookups 409 — name-based callers can be wedged.
push-invoice hardcodes 9%+9% GST and fixed ledger names (GST SALE/CGST/SGST) — wrong for any non-9% rate or differently-named ledgers; silently produces incorrect vouchers.
Process-level uncaughtException handler only logs and keeps serving (index.ts:30) — the instance can continue in a corrupted state after a fatal error.
techDebt: sync.ts is a 2992-line god-file mixing auth, validation, ingest, queue, GCS proxy, dashboard reads, and a full inventory-analytics engine — should be split into modules/services.
Two parallel auth implementations: requireApiKey (auth.ts) and requireClientApiKey (sync.ts:28) duplicate the timingSafeEqual logic; only differ by env var/Supabase client.

SQL is managed as hand-applied, manually-fanned-out migration files (supabase_schema_v2..v6, supabase_new_tables.sql, scan_jobs.sql, push_queue_edit_state.sql) plus a consolidated full_schema.sql — no migration tool, no ordering guarantees; documented drift risk (push_queue.edit_state/push_now missing on a client project per project memory).
Heavy use of `any` and ad-hoc Record<string,unknown> normalization instead of a schema validator (zod/valibot); validation is bespoke per field.
Inventory scenario thresholds, report metadata, and CSV formatting are large literal blocks embedded in the route file rather than a dedicated analytics module/config.
scan_jobs table is defined in SQL and referenced by mobile/parsing over Supabase realtime but the backend never touches it — backend SQL files carry tables the backend doesn't use.
compiled .d.ts and .js-less .ts coexist in src (sync.d.ts etc. checked in alongside .ts), suggesting build artifacts committed into source.
Env var naming is inconsistent/case-sensitive (SUPABASE_URL_Client vs *_CLIENT) and only documented in a code comment — easy to misconfigure on deploy.
Best-effort error swallowing (console.warn/error) in restore, cleanup, sync_log, and GCS paths hides partial-failure states from callers and monitoring.

architecture.component: Parsing / OCR Backend (Flask-style HTTP server on GCP Cloud Run + RunPod serverless GPU workers)
architecture.purpose: Turns scanned/PDF invoices into draft Tally vouchers. A phone/web scan POSTs a PDF to this stateless HTTP service (Cloud Run); it rasterizes the PDF, OCRs it on a RunPod serverless GPU (Nanonets-OCR2-3B for purchase, MiniCPM-V-4.5 for sale), runs a per-vendor regex rule engine + fuzzy match against live Supabase stock/party masters, builds a Tally voucher, and POSTs it to the backend push_queue so the desktop app can push it into TallyPrime. Note: it is built on Python's stdlib http.server (ThreadingHTTPServer), not Flask, despite the prompt naming.

architecture.component: aiaccountant Flutter frontend (mobile/web client for TallyBridge)
architecture.purpose: A Flutter mobile (Android) + web client that lets users photograph/scan sale and purchase invoices, sends them to a Cloud Run parsing service, then reviews/edits the parsed voucher in a live queue and one-tap "pushes" it into TallyPrime via the desktop TallyBridge app. It authenticates users with Firebase Phone Auth and reads/writes the SAME per-tenant Supabase project (e.g. ztugw client-prod) directly over PostgREST + Realtime, while a few report/activate calls go through the Cloud Run backend.

findings.title: Two divergent money-rounding regimes on the SAME invoice data, neither tested
findings.evidence: backend/src/routes/sync.ts:1004-1014 toMoney uses JS float `Number(numeric.toFixed(2))` and toPaise does `Math.round(toMoney(value)*100)`; the parsing voucher path uses Python Decimal with ROUND_HALF_UP — parsing/lib/numeric.py:21-22 round2() and parsing/purchase/voucher_builder.py:1331/1349/1357 (round2 of quantity*rate, subtotal scaling, delta correction). The Flutter/sale path uses Python float round() — parsing/server/handler.py:1232 `amount = round(gross*(1-discount_pct/100.0),2)` and :1271 `cgst = round(subtotal*SALE_GST_RATE,2)`.
findings.impact: A voucher built in parsing (Decimal half-up) and re-ingested through backend (JS toFixed banker-ish float) can disagree by a paise on subtotal/CGST/SGST, producing voucher totals that don't reconcile in Tally and breaking the snapshot/restore equality checks. Float .toFixed(2) also mis-rounds known values (e.g. 1.005 -> '1.00'). No test pins any of these.
findings.recommendation: Write golden-value unit tests FIRST for toMoney/toPaise (Vitest) and round2/build_sale_voucher_payload tax math (pytest), with a shared fixture table of (qty, rate, discount_pct, gst_rate) -> expected subtotal/cgst/sgst/total. Make the assertion that the backend and parsing paths agree to the paise on the same inputs an explicit cross-path test.

findings.title: Ingest is a hand-rolled snapshot+restore, not a transaction, and is completely untested
findings.evidence: backend/src/routes/sync.ts:662 captureVoucherGraphSnapshot, :703 restoreVoucherGraphSnapshot, :595 restoreRows, :443 upsertInBatches with onConflict keys 'company_id,tally_guid' (vouchers/purchases) and 'company_id,name' (groups/ledgers/stock). The restore path only console.error's on failure (per architecture digest). The whole /api/sync handler (sync.ts:~1860-2210) replays many independent PostgREST calls with no DB transaction.
findings.impact: A Cloud Run timeout/OOM (100mb body) mid-ingest leaves vouchers/items/entries half-written; restore is best-effort. Idempotency (re-running the same sync) is the single most important correctness property and nothing verifies that a second identical ingest is a no-op or that a partial failure fully restores.
findings.recommendation: Integration test the ingest against an ephemeral Postgres/Supabase (Testcontainers postgres or a throwaway Supabase branch via the Supabase MCP create_branch): seed a company, POST a recorded /api/sync body twice, assert row counts/values are identical (idempotency), then POST a body that throws mid-way and assert the snapshot fully restores. This is the highest-ROI integration test in the system.

findings.title: Tally voucher XML parsing is pure and trivially fixture-testable, but has zero fixtures
findings.evidence: src/python/xml_parser.py:265 parse_vouchers(xml_text)->list, :178 parse_groups, :209 parse_ledgers, :444 parse_stock, :518 parse_outstanding — all take a raw XML string and return dicts; e.g. quantity parsing at :301-306 splits ACTUALQTY on whitespace ('10 Nos' -> 10.0/'Nos'), discount_pct from DISCOUNT at :308. There are already captured responses in src/python/tally-responses/ and wireshark_requests/ that could seed fixtures, but no test references them.
findings.impact: Any TallyPrime XML layout drift (different ACTUALQTY format, missing field, ISCANCELLED handling at :277, ALLINVENTORYENTRIES vs INVENTORYENTRIES fallback at :293) silently yields wrong qty/rate/amount or dropped items. Because port 9000 is single-threaded and heavy reads FREEZE TallyPrime (documented memory: tally_9000_single_threaded_hang), you must NOT test against live Tally — record/replay is mandatory.
findings.recommendation: Snapshot real Tally XML into src/python/tests/fixtures/*.xml (reuse tally-responses/), then pytest each parse_* against expected dicts. This gives a CI-safe Tally substitute forever, so the desktop sync loop can be tested without TallyPrime.

findings.title: Voucher dedup keys off exact invoice number only — a known duplicate-voucher vector with no test
findings.evidence: parsing/server/handler.py:1723 check_duplicacy(invoice_number) queries Supabase vouchers with params {'voucher_number': f'eq.{invoice_number}'} — exact match only. Sale path generates synthetic numbers SALE-<timestamp> (handler.py:1282) so two scans seconds apart are non-duplicate; OCR-missed numbers (Pidilite 'not detected') bypass dedup entirely (:2042/:2132). Backend upsert onConflict 'company_id,tally_guid' (sync.ts:443/2053) is the only DB-level guard and is untested.
findings.impact: Duplicate purchase/sale vouchers get enqueued into push_queue and pushed into TallyPrime, corrupting the client's books — the exact failure a paying accounting client cannot tolerate.
findings.recommendation: Unit-test check_duplicacy with mocked Supabase responses (empty vs match) and add a table-driven test for normalize_voucher_number (handler.py:1494). Add an integration assertion that enqueuing the same OCR payload twice produces one push_queue row.

findings.title: electron-store one-time migrations are deterministic and untested despite a prior drift incident
findings.evidence: src/main/index.ts:66-71 migratedToHybridV1 flips render->hybrid; :79-82 migratedSyncInterval6hV1 forces 360-min interval. These are pure functions of current store state guarded by a boolean flag. store.ts (176 lines) holds AppConfig defaults. Project memory documents the push_queue.edit_state migration DRIFT that silently broke the client queue — schema/config migrations are a proven failure surface here.
findings.impact: A migration that double-applies, or fails to apply for a config carrying readMode:'shadow' (which Settings can't even re-select — store allows auto|xml-only|hybrid only), changes sync behavior for a live client with no signal.
findings.recommendation: Vitest unit tests over the migration functions with an in-memory electron-store mock: assert idempotency (running twice = once), assert the flag gates re-runs, and assert a value already at target is left untouched. Fast, zero-infra, high confidence.

findings.title: Flutter app has a single stale test that cannot pass in CI; the money/tax god-file is untested
findings.evidence: aiaccountant/test/widget_test.dart asserts find.text('ABC Traders')/'Today'/'Camera' against a shell that now seeds only sale rows from seed_data and pumps Supabase/Firebase with no mocks. The real risk surface — voucher_detail_sheet.dart (~3500 lines mixing payload parse, tax math, Supabase writes, HTTP push) — has no tests; pubspec dev_dependencies has only flutter_test + flutter_lints (no mockito/mocktail).
findings.impact: The on-device tax recomputation and push payload assembly can drift from the backend/parsing math with nothing to catch it; the only existing test is a false signal (red or skipped).
findings.recommendation: Delete/replace widget_test.dart. Extract pure tax/payload functions out of voucher_detail_sheet.dart into a testable lib file and cover them with flutter_test; add mocktail for Supabase/Firebase so widget tests can run headless in CI.

production.currentState: The system is NOT production-ready from a security standpoint and currently carries at least one critical, internet-exposed secret leak. Auth on the Express backend is structurally sound at the transport level (constant-time API-key compare via timingSafeEqual + length guard, Firebase JWT verification, every route mounts requireApiKey/requireClientApiKey), but the model collapses to a SINGLE shared static API key with NO per-company authorization, so any key holder can read or mutate any tenant's data. Multi-tenant isolation rests entirely on per-client Supabase projects plus manual company_id WHERE filters in a 2992-line god-file; the actual RLS policies shipped are all permissive `USING(true) WITH CHECK(true)` with no role/predicate, so the publishable/anon key used by the Flutter app grants full read/update/delete on push_queue, vouchers, scan_jobs, etc. The OCR/parsing Cloud Run service has NO authentication at all. CORS on the backend is wide open (`cors()` with no allowlist). The local push server on 3002 correctly rejects non-loopback peers but is itself unauthenticated. The Electron installer (NSIS) is NOT code-signed and auto-updates from a PUBLIC GitHub repo. Concrete confirmed leak: backend/.env (SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY=service_role, API_KEY, FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_B64) and parsing/.env (service_role + RunPod key + Firebase service account) were committed and remain in the history of the PUBLIC github.com/siddharthniranjan2003/TallyBridge repo (commits 0b536fe and ae5872a, reachable from origin/* branches; 5 secret-material hits in committed diffs). On-disk values differ from the oldest committed values (suggesting partial rotation), but the secrets are permanently in public history and must be treated as compromised. aiaccountant kept its secrets out of git (good): .env, config.dart, google-services.json, firebase_options.dart are all gitignored and untracked, though the AiAccountant GitHub repo is also PUBLIC and ships hardcoded publishable keys (lower risk by design, but they point at a real project).

findings.title: service_role + Firebase + API_KEY secrets committed to a PUBLIC GitHub repo's git history
findings.evidence: git log --all -- backend/.env parsing/.env shows adds at 0b536fe (backend/.env) and ae5872a (parsing/.env). `git branch -r --contains 0b536fe/ae5872a` lists origin/TallyBridge-Backend-Refactor and 5 other origin/* branches. `gh repo view siddharthniranjan2003/TallyBridge` => PUBLIC. JWT payload decode of the committed SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY => "role":"service_role"; `git log --all -p -- *.env | grep -c 'service_role|private_key|eyJ'` => 5. Files contain SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY, API_KEY (service secret), FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_B64, RUNPOD_POD_API_KEY.
findings.impact: Anyone on the internet can clone the public repo, run `git log -p`, and extract a service_role Supabase key (full DB read/write/delete that BYPASSES RLS), the backend API_KEY (full backend access), the RunPod API key (GPU spend), and the Firebase service account (mint tokens / impersonate any user). This is total compromise of the testing tenant (yynuu) and, if the same secret class was ever committed for client prod, of ztugw. Even though on-disk values now differ (partial rotation), the keys are permanently in public history.
findings.recommendation: Treat ALL committed secrets as compromised: immediately rotate the Supabase service_role key (yynuu and any client project), backend API_KEY/API_KEY_CLIENT, RunPod API key, and regenerate the Firebase service account key. Purge history with git filter-repo (or BFG) on every branch and force-push, then invalidate any forks/clones; or make the repo private and rotate regardless. Decouple auto-update publishing from the source repo so the source can be made private. Add a pre-commit secret scanner (gitleaks/trufflehog) and a CI gate.

findings.title: All shipped RLS policies are permissive USING(true) WITH CHECK(true) with no role/tenant predicate
findings.evidence: backend/supabase_new_tables.sql:57-87, supabase_scan_jobs.sql:47-48, supabase_schema_v2.sql:93-96 — every CREATE POLICY is `FOR ALL USING (true) WITH CHECK (true)` with no `TO <role>` clause (so applies to PUBLIC incl. anon/authenticated) and no auth.uid()/company_id predicate. full_schema.sql defines company_id columns but contains ZERO `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`/`CREATE POLICY`. Flutter (lib/main.dart:27-29) initializes Supabase with the publishable/anon key and writes directly: voucher_detail_sheet.dart:650-651 .update, :787 .delete().eq('id', rowId), queue_screen.dart:174 .from('push_queue').
findings.impact: Within a tenant's Supabase project, the publishable/anon key grants full SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE on push_queue, vouchers, scan_jobs and report tables to ANY caller who knows the table shape and a row id. There is no isolation between users of the same client, and a single shared/leaked anon key plus a known row id lets an attacker edit voucher payloads (financial tampering) or delete queued pushes. The 'one Supabase project per client' boundary is the ONLY real isolation; a single config mistake pointing two tenants at one project leaks everything.
findings.recommendation: Replace blanket USING(true) policies with predicate-scoped policies (e.g. company_id IN (SELECT company_id FROM user_companies WHERE user_id = auth.uid())) and scope the permissive service_role policy to `TO service_role` only. For anon/authenticated roles, restrict writes to push_queue.voucher_payload to rows the user owns; never allow client DELETE on financial rows. Add a CI check that fails on any USING(true) policy. Verify with Supabase get_advisors (security lints).

findings.title: Parsing / OCR Cloud Run service exposes invoice ingest with NO authentication
findings.evidence: grep across parsing/*.py for x-api-key/authorization/bearer/Access-Control/401/403 on the HTTP handlers returns nothing on the parse path (only test_minicpm.py uses a Supabase bearer). Architecture digest + handoff notes confirm x-api-key was reverted; scan_uploader sends only Content-Type: application/pdf. Service runs on stdlib ThreadingHTTPServer.
findings.impact: Anyone who learns a tallybridge-parsing-*.run.app URL can submit arbitrary PDFs: drives unbounded RunPod GPU spend (DoS-by-cost), and—because the parser enqueues into push_queue—can inject attacker-controlled draft vouchers that a user may one-tap push into TallyPrime. Combined with the weak duplicacy check (exact voucher_number eq only), forged/duplicate purchase vouchers can be planted.
findings.recommendation: Require a shared secret (x-api-key with timingSafeEqual) or Firebase-verified bearer on all parse endpoints; reject unauthenticated requests with 401. Put the service behind Cloud Run IAM / an API gateway and restrict ingress. Add a request-size and rate limit, and a per-tenant quota on RunPod jobs.

findings.title: Single shared API_KEY grants cross-tenant write; push-results / push-queue activate have no company scoping
findings.evidence: auth.ts uses one process.env.API_KEY for all of /api/sync/*. sync.ts:2513 /push-results updates push_queue `.eq('id', id)` with NO company_id filter and NO ownership check, accepting arbitrary `tally_response` JSON. sync.ts:2393 /push-queue/activate and 2362 image endpoint are keyed by id; activate treats company identity as optional.
findings.impact: Any holder of the (shared, and historically leaked) API_KEY can mark ANY company's queued voucher pushed/failed, inject arbitrary tally_response payloads, activate/deactivate any job, and fetch any invoice image by id — across every company in that backend's reach. There is no service-to-service identity separation between the desktop connector, parsing service, and Flutter app.
findings.recommendation: Move to per-tenant (or per-component) keys, or derive identity from the Firebase token and enforce company ownership on every push_queue mutation (add a company_id check in the WHERE clause and validate it against the caller's allowed companies). Reject /push-results entries whose row company_id is not owned by the caller. Consider signed, short-lived service tokens instead of a static shared key.

findings.title: Electron NSIS installer is unsigned and auto-updates from a public repo
findings.evidence: package.json build.win has only target+icon; no certificateFile/certificateSha1/signingHashAlgorithms and no CSC_LINK/CSC_KEY_PASSWORD usage anywhere in the repo. electron-builder.yml publish => provider github, repo TallyBridge (PUBLIC). Auto-update via electron-updater (MEMORY: live GitHub auto-update on public repo).
findings.impact: Windows SmartScreen will warn on every install (poor trust for a paid client), and—more seriously—an unsigned binary distributed via a public release channel has weaker tamper guarantees. Anyone with push access to the public releases (or who can MITM/typo-squat) could distribute a malicious build; users have no signature to validate. The app runs a local server and pushes data into Tally, so a trojaned build is high-impact.
findings.recommendation: Obtain an OV/EV code-signing certificate, set win.certificateFile + CSC_KEY_PASSWORD (or Azure Trusted Signing), and enable forceCodeSigning so unsigned builds fail the pipeline. Sign the auto-update artifacts and verify signatures on update. Restrict who can publish releases; move releases to a dedicated repo separate from source.

findings.title: Local push server on 127.0.0.1:3002 is unauthenticated (loopback-only, but any local process can push vouchers into Tally)
findings.evidence: local-push-server.ts:176-179 rejects non-loopback remoteAddress (so a remote LAN attacker cannot connect — good), but there is no token/secret check on POST /push-voucher (lines 193-214). Company defaults to the single enabled company if not specified (pickCompanyName 87-97).
findings.impact: Any process or page that can reach localhost on the user's machine (malware, a malicious Electron/Node app, or a browser via DNS-rebinding tricks where the Host check is absent) can POST a voucher and have it pushed into TallyPrime. The loopback guard blocks LAN attackers but not local ones, and there is no shared-secret handshake with the backend poller.
findings.recommendation: Require a per-session shared secret (generated at startup, stored in electron-store, sent by the trusted poller as a header and compared with timingSafeEqual). Validate the Host header to mitigate DNS-rebinding. Keep the loopback bind. Optionally bind to a random high port and pass it to the trusted caller out-of-band.

findings.title: Wide-open CORS and no schema validation on the 100MB /api/sync ingest
findings.evidence: backend/src/index.ts:16 `app.use(cors())` with no origin/allowlist/credentials config. Body limit 100mb (index.ts:10-13). sync.ts is 2992 lines using heavy `any`/ad-hoc Record<string,unknown> normalization, bespoke per-field validation, and the ingest is a hand-rolled snapshot+rollback across many PostgREST calls (not a real transaction).
findings.impact: Open CORS lets any website issue authenticated cross-origin requests (relevant if a Firebase session/token can be replayed from a browser). The 100MB unvalidated body plus per-field hand-rolled parsing is a large attack/footgun surface: malformed input can partially write the voucher graph (vouchers/items/entries half-replaced) with only best-effort console.error rollback, risking data corruption rather than a clean rejection.
findings.recommendation: Set an explicit CORS allowlist (Flutter web origin + dashboard) and disable wildcard with credentials. Adopt a schema validator (zod/valibot) at the route boundary for /api/sync and push endpoints; reject on parse failure before any DB write. Lower the body limit to the real maximum and stream-validate. Wrap ingest in a real DB transaction (Postgres function/RPC) so partial writes cannot persist.

findings.title: aiaccountant ships hardcoded publishable Supabase keys and points default env at a live project
findings.evidence: lib/core/config.dart:18-47 hardcodes sb_publishable_* keys as defaultValue and supabaseUrl defaultValue=https://yynuuysvjeipawzfbeme.supabase.co. config.dart, .env, google-services.json, firebase_options.dart are all untracked/gitignored (verified). AiAccountant GitHub repo is PUBLIC.
findings.impact: Publishable/anon keys are public-by-design and safe ONLY if RLS is correct — which it is NOT (see permissive-RLS finding), so these keys become a real lever for tenant data access. Defaulting to the yynuu testing project means a misbuilt prod binary talks to the testing DB (digest notes prod env is a placeholder still on yynuu).
findings.recommendation: Keep publishable keys but make RLS enforcement the dependency it claims to be (per the comment in config.dart). Remove live-project defaults so a build without --dart-define fails fast instead of silently hitting testing. Gate the prod flavor behind a real prod Supabase + Firebase project before shipping.

recommendations: EMERGENCY (do first, hours not days): rotate every secret that was ever committed — Supabase service_role keys (yynuu + all client projects), backend API_KEY/API_KEY_CLIENT, RUNPOD_POD_API_KEY, and regenerate the Firebase service account. Assume the public-history values are compromised.

Purge backend/.env and parsing/.env from git history (git filter-repo/BFG) across ALL branches and force-push; or make the source repo private. Decouple electron auto-update releases from the source repo so source can go private.

Fix RLS: replace every `USING(true) WITH CHECK(true)` policy with company/auth.uid()-scoped predicates, scope service_role-only policies `TO service_role`, and forbid anon DELETE/UPDATE on financial rows. Run Supabase get_advisors and gate CI on any USING(true) policy.
Add authentication to the parsing Cloud Run service (x-api-key timingSafeEqual or Firebase bearer) plus rate/size limits and per-tenant RunPod quotas; put it behind Cloud Run IAM ingress controls.

Replace the single shared API_KEY with per-component/per-tenant credentials and enforce company_id ownership on every push_queue mutation (especially /push-results, /push-queue/activate, image fetch).
Add a startup-generated shared secret to the local push server (3002) and validate the Host header to defend against local-process abuse and DNS-rebinding.
Code-sign the NSIS installer (OV/EV cert or Azure Trusted Signing) with forceCodeSigning, and sign+verify auto-update artifacts; restrict who can publish releases.
Lock down CORS to an explicit origin allowlist and introduce schema validation (zod) on /api/sync + push routes; wrap ingest in a real DB transaction/RPC instead of best-effort snapshot rollback.
Add automated secret scanning (gitleaks/trufflehog) as a pre-commit hook and CI gate so this class of leak cannot recur — there is currently no CI at all.
toolingChoices: gitleaks or trufflehog — pre-commit hook + CI secret scanning to prevent re-committing .env/keys (the repo has none today)
git-filter-repo (preferred over BFG) — purge .env blobs from full git history across all branches
Supabase RLS + get_advisors security lints — replace USING(true) policies with auth.uid()/company_id predicates and lint them in CI
zod (or valibot) — schema validation at the Express route boundary, replacing the bespoke `any`-based per-field normalization in sync.ts
Azure Trusted Signing or an OV/EV code-signing certificate wired via electron-builder win.certificateFile + CSC_KEY_PASSWORD with forceCodeSigning
Google Secret Manager (or GCP Cloud Run secret env bindings) — source backend/parsing secrets at deploy time instead of committed .env/backend.env.yaml
helmet + an explicit cors allowlist on the Express app to replace bare cors() and add standard security headers
express-rate-limit (backend) and a Cloud Run concurrency/quota limit on the parsing service to bound abuse and RunPod GPU cost
production.effort: Secret rotation + history purge: M (1-2 days incl. coordinating Supabase/Firebase/RunPod key rollover across yynuu + client projects and redeploys). RLS hardening across per-client projects: L (fan-out per tenant, plus testing every Flutter write path). Per-tenant auth / push_queue ownership scoping in the 2992-line sync.ts: L. Parsing service auth + rate limiting: S-M. Local push 3002 shared secret + Host check: S. CORS allowlist + helmet: S. zod validation on ingest: M. Code signing setup: S-M (cert procurement is the long pole). CI + secret scanning bootstrap (none exists): M.

production.currentState:
There is zero CI/CD. No .github/workflows exists in either repo; the backend test script is literally `echo "Error: no test specified" && exit 1`. Every build, sign, release, and deploy across all five components is a manual, copy-pasted shell sequence captured only in untracked scratch files (TallyBridge/command.txt, aiaccountant/command.txt) — not in any committed, reviewable, reproducible pipeline.

Release/deploy surface by component:
- Electron desktop: `npm run build:python` (PyInstaller --onefile) -> set GH_TOKEN from `gh auth token` -> `npm run build` -> `npx electron-builder --publish always` -> then MANUALLY `gh release edit vX --draft=false`. Auto-update is electron-updater pointed at public GitHub repo siddharthniranjan2003/TallyBridge. Installer is UNSIGNED.
- Backend (Cloud Run): `gcloud config configurations activate <env>` then `gcloud run deploy tallybridge-backend --source backend --region asia-south1 --project <projnum>`, per environment. Manual project switching; documented gotchas (new revision serves 0% traffic, push-queue key 401) are tribal knowledge.
- Parsing (Cloud Run): same `gcloud run deploy --source parsing` pattern; Dockerfile still carries Render-era env names (MINICPM_HTTP_HOST, "so Render can route") despite Cloud Run.
- Flutter (aiaccountant): MOST mature piece — product flavors (staging/deployment/prod), `--dart-define-from-file=env/<flavor>.json`, per-flavor google-services.json, gitignored release keystore with debug fallback, .firebaserc aliases. Still hand-driven.
- Supabase: BETTER than digest implied — a real supabase/migrations/ dir with timestamped migrations plus scripts/deploy-supabase-direct-ingest.ps1. But NO supabase/config.toml, the .temp/ link-state (pointing at yynuu testing) is committed to git, legacy backend/*.sql still coexists, and fan-out across client projects is one manual `supabase link` per project.

Net: nothing is gated, nothing is reproducible from a clean checkout, versions are hand-bumped in 3+ disconnected places, and promotion testing->client-prod is "activate the right gcloud config and don't fat-finger the project flag." Least-automated, most error-prone dimension for a paying-client ship.

findings.title: Electron installer is unsigned; auto-update ships unsigned binaries to a paying client
findings.evidence: electron-builder.yml has no win.certificateFile/azureSignToolOptions; package.json build.win has no signing config; repo-wide grep for signtool/cscLink/CSC_LINK/certificate* hits only node_modules. final_deployment/tallybridge-client-handoff-checklist.md:81 lists 'Code-sign the installer to reduce SmartScreen friction' as an OPEN item. Release is `npx electron-builder --publish always` (command.txt:4) with no signing step.
findings.impact: Windows SmartScreen/Defender flags every install AND every auto-update of an unsigned NSIS exe, eroding client trust and risking blocked/quarantined updates. Unsigned electron-updater downloads weaken update integrity. Recurring per-update friction, not one-time.

Wire signing into electron-builder via win.signtoolOptions/Azure Trusted Signing, cert fed from a CI secret (CSC_LINK/CSC_KEY_PASSWORD). Sign both installer and bundled tallybridge-engine.exe inside a GitHub Actions windows-latest job so the cert never lives on a dev laptop.

findings.title: electron-builder config duplicated and divergent across package.json and electron-builder.yml; bare invocation silently ignores the .yml
findings.evidence: Two configs: package.json build{} (appId, win.nsis, extraResources) and electron-builder.yml (same fields PLUS publish:{provider:github, owner:siddharthniranjan2003, repo:TallyBridge} and installerIcon). command.txt:4 runs `npx electron-builder` with NO -c flag. Project memory electron_builder_config_gotcha: bare electron-builder uses package.json build block, ignores the .yml; publish repo inferred from git origin unless -c passed. package.json build{} has NO publish key.
findings.impact: Actual publish target depends on git origin at release time, not the explicit owner/repo in the .yml — a footgun if origin points at a fork/wrong remote. installerIcon and copyright in the .yml are silently dropped. Two sources of truth drift; whichever a future maintainer edits may not be the one that runs.
findings.recommendation: Pick ONE config file. Recommend deleting package.json build{} and always invoking `electron-builder -c electron-builder.yml`, OR delete the .yml and fold publish/installerIcon into package.json. Fix the invocation in the CI job so it is explicit and reviewed.

findings.title: No automated build/test gate anywhere; backend test is exit 1; releases ship straight from a dev machine
findings.evidence: No .github/workflows in either repo (Glob .github/** -> none). backend/package.json:7 test=`echo "Error: no test specified" && exit 1`. Releases use local `gh auth token` + `npx electron-builder --publish always`. Deploys use local `gcloud run deploy --source` after manual `gcloud config configurations activate`. Current branch has 6 modified + dozens of untracked uncommitted files.
findings.impact: A broken tsc build, a missing PyInstaller hidden import, or an uncommitted mitigation (memory client_1211_freeze_rca: HEAD 5b37f7a regresses, mitigations uncommitted) can reach a client because nothing compiles/lints/tests on a clean checkout before publish.
findings.recommendation: Stand up 4 GitHub Actions workflows: (1) electron-release on tag (windows-latest: npm ci, build:python, build, sign, electron-builder --publish always); (2) backend-deploy (tsc typecheck, deploy via Workload Identity Federation, then update-traffic --to-latest); (3) parsing-deploy (mirror); (4) flutter-build (flavor matrix + flutter analyze). Gate each on at least tsc --noEmit / flutter analyze before real tests land.

findings.title: Cloud Run 0% traffic and push-queue key 401 gotchas are unmitigated manual steps
findings.evidence: Project memory parsing_gcp_redeploy_gotchas: after redeploying tallybridge-parsing the new revision serves 0% (must run update-traffic --to-latest) and the push-queue API key can break (401); smoke-test one enqueue. command.txt:14-20 shows raw `gcloud run deploy` with no follow-up traffic-shift or smoke test. backend/parsing Dockerfiles use unpinned npm install / pip install.
findings.impact: A deploy can silently serve the OLD revision (0% to new) so a fix appears deployed but isn't, or break parsing->push-queue auth so scanned invoices stop enqueuing — both invisible without a manual smoke test easy to skip under pressure. For a paying client this is a live data-flow outage waiting to happen.
findings.recommendation: In deploy workflows always append `gcloud run services update-traffic <svc> --to-latest` plus a post-deploy smoke step (curl health; for parsing enqueue one canary and assert a push_queue row). Pin deps: backend uses npm ci with committed lockfile in the image; parsing pins requirements.txt.

findings.title: Per-client Supabase migration fan-out is fully manual; no config.toml, committed link-state, legacy SQL coexists with real migrations
findings.evidence: supabase/migrations/ has 6 timestamped migrations (e.g. 20260619_stock_items_part_code.sql) — good — but NO supabase/config.toml (ls -> missing). supabase/.temp/linked-project.json is committed and pins ref yynuuysvjeipawzfbeme (testing). scripts/deploy-supabase-direct-ingest.ps1 does `supabase link --project-ref` + db push per project. Legacy backend/*.sql (supabase_schema_v2..v6, push_queue_edit_state.sql, full_schema.sql) still exist. Memory push_queue_migration_drift: client prod ztugw was MISSING push_queue.edit_state/push_now -> app showed empty queue (400 swallowed).
findings.impact: Each new client requires a human to re-link and db-push with no record of which migration version each client project is on — the documented ztugw drift already caused a silent production failure. As clients grow this is the highest-likelihood production incident source. The committed .temp link-state defaults the script to the wrong (testing) project.
findings.recommendation: Standardize on Supabase CLI migrations (already half-adopted): add a committed supabase/config.toml, gitignore supabase/.temp/, retire legacy backend/*.sql once parity is confirmed. Build a fan-out workflow iterating a committed registry of client project-refs running `supabase db push` against each, with schema_migrations as the version ledger. Run via GitHub Actions with project-refs+db passwords as secrets. Add a post-migration get_advisors drift check.

findings.title: deploy-supabase-direct-ingest.ps1 has a fatal syntax bug: param() after Set-StrictMode
findings.evidence: scripts/deploy-supabase-direct-ingest.ps1:1-13 is `$ErrorActionPreference=...; Set-StrictMode -Version Latest; param(...)`. In PowerShell, param() must be the FIRST statement in a script/function; placing it after executable statements is a parse error, so the script cannot run as written.
findings.impact: The one piece of migration automation that exists is non-functional, which is likely WHY fan-out is still done by hand. Anyone reaching for it hits a parse error and falls back to manual supabase link/db push.
findings.recommendation: Move the param() block to line 1 (before $ErrorActionPreference/Set-StrictMode), then promote this into the CI fan-out job. Verify with `pwsh -NoProfile -File` before trusting it.

findings.title: Android applicationId is the placeholder com.example.aiaccountant with the scaffold TODO still present
findings.evidence: aiaccountant/android/app/build.gradle.kts:21 namespace='com.example.aiaccountant'; :36 applicationId='com.example.aiaccountant' with :35 '// TODO: Specify your own unique Application ID'. All three flavors share this id (comment at :54-58 confirms same applicationId).
findings.impact: Shipping a paying client an app under com.example.* is unprofessional, can collide on Play/devices, and cannot be changed later without a fresh install + re-auth for all users. It couples to release identity (signing/upload keys are bound to the id).
findings.recommendation: Set a real reverse-DNS applicationId (e.g. com.<vendor>.tallybridge) BEFORE first client distribution; ideally distinct ids per flavor so testing/deployment/prod coexist on one device. Update namespace, google-services.json package_name, and Firebase app registration to match.

findings.title: Version numbers hand-bumped in disconnected places with no single source of truth or tag-driven release
findings.evidence: TallyBridge package.json:3 version 1.2.13; aiaccountant/pubspec.yaml:19 version 1.0.0+30; backend/package.json:2 version 1.0.0 (stale, never bumped). Release un-drafting is a separate manual `gh release edit vX --draft=false` (command.txt:8). No CHANGELOG, no tag-driven release.
findings.impact: electron-updater compares versions to decide updates; a missed package.json bump means clients never see a release, or re-publishing the same version confuses the updater. Backend/parsing surface no version at all, so 'which revision is live' is unknowable from the artifact.
findings.recommendation: Drive releases from git tags (vX.Y.Z) with CI reading the tag as the single version source (inject into package.json/pubspec at build). Add a /version or build-SHA header to backend & parsing. Adopt a minimal CHANGELOG and fold un-drafting into the release workflow.

findings.title: PyInstaller engine build is fragile, undocumented, and unverified in any pipeline
findings.evidence: package.json:10 build:python is a single long `pyinstaller --onefile` line with manual --collect-all xmltodict/requests/dotenv and --add-data definitions;definitions. Invoked by hand (command.txt:1) before electron-builder, which expects python-dist/tallybridge-engine.exe (electron-builder.yml:17). No requirements pinning for the build env.
findings.impact: If a new Python dep is added but not added to --collect-all/--hidden-import, the onefile exe silently misses a module and the sync engine crashes ONLY on the client (works in dev where the interpreter is present). Because nothing builds it in CI, a forgotten build:python ships a stale engine inside a fresh installer.
findings.recommendation: Move build:python into the Electron CI job (rebuilt from a pinned src/python/requirements.txt). Add a post-build smoke test running the exe with a no-op/--version flag asserting clean exit + the final JSON line, catching missing-import regressions before publish.

findings.title: Secrets-in-build hygiene: personal GH_TOKEN, committed parsing/.env, committed supabase/.temp leak creds/state into the manual flow
findings.evidence: command.txt:2 `$env:GH_TOKEN = (gh auth token)` — release uses a developer's personal GitHub token. parsing/.env (service_role + RunPod + Firebase key) is committed to git history (.gcloudignore/.dockerignore exclude .env from the IMAGE but not from git). supabase/.temp/linked-project.json (org/project ref) is committed.
findings.impact: Releases tie to one person's credentials (bus factor + over-broad scope), and any local build can accidentally bundle committed secret files. The committed link-state defaults migration tooling to the testing project, inviting wrong-target pushes.
findings.recommendation: Run release/deploy in CI with scoped secrets (a release-only GitHub PAT, GCP Workload Identity Federation instead of long-lived keys, Supabase creds as Actions secrets). Gitignore supabase/.temp/. Rotate the committed parsing/.env credentials and purge from history (coordinated with the parsing-dimension remediation).
