production.currentState: The system has thin, ad-hoc observability and is NOT production-ready on this dimension for a paying client. There is NO crash reporting (zero Sentry/crashReporter across Electron, backend, parsing, or Flutter), NO alerting, and NO automated detection of failures. Logging is unstructured/string-based in most places: the Electron file logger (logger.ts) writes plain `[ts][LEVEL] msg` lines with 5MB rotation keeping only one .old file, and monkey-patches console.* globally. The one bright spot is remote-log.ts, which forwards the in-app Sync Log to BetterStack Live Tail with structured JSON records (level, company, tally_guid, app_version, device) — but it ships the same human-readable strings as `message`, derives level by regex (`/[err|error/i`), and is the ONLY remote telemetry; it is intentionally best-effort (all errors swallowed) and conveys nothing when the app crashes or never reaches a sync. Resilience is weak: cloud_pusher.py has NO retry/backoff/idempotency on any network call (the lone sleep is a post-ReadTimeout verify poll); a single failed window/chunk aborts the run. The /api/sync ingest is a hand-rolled snapshot+rollback across many separate PostgREST calls (not a DB transaction), and restore is itself best-effort, only console.error-ing on failure (sync.ts:591,602,755). Health checks exist but are useless for monitoring: backend `/health` (index.ts:23), parsing `/health` (handler.py:1792), and local-push `/health` all return a STATIC `{status:ok}` with zero dependency checks (no Supabase/RunPod/Tally probe), so an uptime check stays green while Supabase is down. Graceful degradation is partial: Tally port pre-flight skips sync when Tally is down, and cloud_pusher maps connection errors to typed statuses — but failures mostly surface only as a red company row + a sync-log line on the CLIENT's screen, invisible to the operator unless they happen to be watching BetterStack. The known 1.2.11 freeze (full-FY catch-up on single-threaded Tally) had no telemetry that would have flagged it; mitigation was a blunt 6h interval default. There is no CI and no tests (backend test = `exit 1`).

findings.title: No crash reporting anywhere (no Sentry) — production failures are invisible to the operator
findings.evidence: grep for sentry/crashReporter across repo: only matches in docs/HTML, none in src/main, backend/src, parsing, or aiaccountant. Electron has no crashReporter.start(); backend index.ts:27-32 only console.error's unhandledRejection/uncaughtException; parsing handler.py:2209 returns traceback in the HTTP body to the caller, not to any sink.
findings.impact: When the desktop connector crashes on a client machine, a Cloud Run instance throws, or the Flutter app errors, no one is notified and there is no stack-trace aggregation. Mean-time-to-detection for a paying-client incident is effectively 'until the client complains.' The 1.2.11 freeze is the canonical example — it shipped and froze clients with no automated signal.
findings.recommendation: Add Sentry to all three+1 surfaces: @sentry/electron (main+renderer) with crashReporter, @sentry/node in backend/src/index.ts wrapping the Express app, sentry_flutter in aiaccountant, and a sentry-sdk init in the parsing http.server. Tag events with company/tally_guid/app_version (already available in remote-log context) and ingest_mode so client incidents are attributable.

findings.title: Health endpoints are static 200s with no dependency probe — uptime monitoring would be falsely green
findings.evidence: backend/src/index.ts:23 `res.json({status:'ok'})`; parsing handler.py:1792-1807 returns static 'healthy'; local-push-server.ts:183 returns static ok. None query Supabase, RunPod, or GCS.
findings.impact: A GCP uptime check or load-balancer health probe passes while Supabase is unreachable, the RunPod GPU endpoint is cold/dead, or the service role key is wrong (the documented yynuu RLS-returns-200-[] and push_queue column-drift failure modes). Outages stay undetected until ingest/parse traffic fails for real users.
findings.recommendation: Make /health a real readiness check: backend pings Supabase (cheap select on a known table) and returns 503 on failure; parsing checks RunPod endpoint reachability and the configured Supabase project; add a separate /livez (process up) vs /readyz (deps ok). Wire GCP Cloud Run uptime checks + an alerting policy on both services.

findings.title: No retry/backoff/idempotency on cloud push network calls — transient failures abort the whole sync
findings.evidence: cloud_pusher.py: _post_sync_payload and the direct PostgREST path issue a single requests.post; ConnectionError/ReadTimeout/HTTPError each return ok:False immediately with no retry. push() aborts on the first failed chunk (lines 875-907). Only sleep in file is the verify poll (line 636).
findings.impact: A momentary Cloud Run cold start, 503, or network blip during a multi-chunk voucher upload fails the entire run; the client sees a red row and must wait for the next 6h cycle. Worse, the ingest is non-transactional, so a mid-chunk failure can leave the company half-written (vouchers persisted, masters not, or vice versa).
findings.recommendation: Add bounded exponential backoff with jitter (e.g. 3 attempts on 5xx/timeout/connection error) around each POST in cloud_pusher, and make ingest idempotent via the existing alter_ids/synced_at markers so a retried chunk is a safe no-op. Treat 4xx (auth/validation) as non-retryable.

findings.title: Swallowed-error patterns hide real failures (column-missing 400, malformed Python JSON reported as success)
findings.evidence: sync-engine.ts:455-457 — JSON.parse failure of the Python result only console.errors and falls back to PREVIOUS record counts while still reporting status 'success' (line 465). Backend restore failures only console.error (sync.ts:591,602,755). remote-log/logger writes are fully try/caught to no-op. Per project memory, a missing push_queue.edit_state/push_now column caused a swallowed 400 → app queue silently showed empty.
findings.impact: A failed or partial sync can be reported to the client as a successful sync with stale counts, eroding trust in the numbers. The push_queue column-drift case already shipped to client-prod (ztugw) and silently broke the queue with no error visible anywhere.
findings.recommendation: On Python-result JSON parse failure, mark the run as error (not success) and ship the raw tail to BetterStack/Sentry. In the backend, escalate restore/rollback failures to error-level structured events (data-integrity alarm), and surface column/schema 400s instead of swallowing — withSupabaseSchemaGuidance (sync.ts:1315) already detects them; route those to an alert.

findings.title: Non-transactional ingest with best-effort rollback risks silent partial writes
findings.evidence: sync.ts uses snapshot+restore across many separate PostgREST calls (restoreVoucherGraphSnapshot:703, restoreRows:595, rollbackInsertedRows); restore on the catch path (2231-2249) and its helpers only console.error on failure. Cloud Run has request time/body (100mb) limits that can kill mid-ingest.
findings.impact: A Cloud Run timeout/OOM or a failed restore between steps leaves the tenant's voucher graph or snapshot sections half-replaced, and nothing alerts on it. For a financial sync this is a correctness hazard, not just availability.
findings.recommendation: Move the multi-table ingest into a single Postgres RPC/transaction (the direct path already calls tb_ingest_* RPCs — converge render mode onto a transactional RPC too). Emit a structured 'ingest_partial' error event whenever a restore helper fails, and add a post-ingest consistency check (record_counts vs persisted rows).

findings.title: Client-side failures only surface on the client's own screen — no operator-facing aggregation or alerting
findings.evidence: sync-engine.ts:481-493 sets lastSyncStatus:'error' and emits 'company-error' to the renderer (red row + sync-log line). The only off-device path is remote-log.ts to BetterStack Live Tail, which is a passive tail with no alerting and ships only when the app is running and reaches a sync.
findings.impact: For a paying client there is no proactive 'this client hasn't synced in 24h' or 'this client is erroring repeatedly' signal. Operators learn of problems reactively. StatusBar additionally lies (cosmetic countdown, hardcoded internetOk=true) so even the client's own UI under-reports connectivity issues.
findings.recommendation: Add a lightweight heartbeat: have the connector POST a sync outcome (ok/error/skipped + counts + last_synced_at) to the backend each run; build a BetterStack/Grafana alert (or a scheduled Cloud Run job) on 'no heartbeat in N hours' and 'error rate > X' per company. Define one structured event schema shared by Electron, backend, and Flutter.

findings.title: Parse/ingest endpoints unauthenticated + committed secrets compound the resilience risk
findings.evidence: Per digest and handler.py, parse endpoints take no auth; parsing/.env (service_role + RunPod + Firebase key) is in git history. push-results (sync.ts) updates push_queue by id with no tenant scoping.
findings.impact: Beyond security, this is a resilience/observability gap: anyone hitting the URL can drive unbounded RunPod GPU spend and enqueue garbage vouchers, and there is no rate limit, no abuse alerting, and no per-tenant error attribution to detect it.
findings.recommendation: Gate parse + push-results behind the existing API key, scope push_queue mutations by company, add rate limiting, and emit structured auth-failure / spend events that feed the alerting layer. (Rotate the committed credentials — covered under the Security dimension.)

findings.title: Unstructured string logging + global console monkey-patch makes machine analysis hard
findings.evidence: logger.ts:39-48 writes plain `[ts][LEVEL] msg` and initLogger() reassigns console.log/warn/error globally (lines 64-77). remote-log derives level via regex on the message string (remote-log.ts:101). Backend/parsing use bare console.error/print.
findings.impact: No correlation IDs, no per-run/per-company structured fields in the file log, and level is guessed from text — so querying 'all errors for company X in run Y' is impossible. Log rotation keeps only one .old file (5MB), so a chatty incident's history is lost.
findings.recommendation: Adopt one structured JSON logging standard (e.g. pino for Node main+backend, structlog or stdlib logging with JSON formatter for Python) with shared fields: run_id, company/tally_guid, ingest_mode, app_version, level. Stop guessing level from message text; keep N rotated files.

recommendations: Add Sentry across all four surfaces before client ship: @sentry/electron (main+renderer, with crashReporter) in src/main, @sentry/node wrapping Express in backend/src/index.ts, sentry-sdk in parsing/server, sentry_flutter in aiaccountant. Tag every event with company/tally_guid/app_version/ingest_mode (already on the remote-log context object).

Make all three /health endpoints real readiness checks (backend→Supabase ping, parsing→RunPod+Supabase, returning 503 on failure) and split /livez vs /readyz; then create GCP Cloud Run uptime checks + alerting policies on the backend and parsing services.

Add bounded exponential-backoff-with-jitter retries (3 attempts, retry only 5xx/timeout/connection) around every POST in cloud_pusher.py, and make ingest idempotent via alter_ids/synced_at so retried chunks are safe no-ops.

Fix the silent-success bugs: on Python-result JSON parse failure (sync-engine.ts:455) mark the run as error and ship the raw tail; escalate backend restore/rollback failures (sync.ts:591/602/755) and schema/column 400s to error-level structured events instead of console.error/swallow.

Convert the render-mode ingest to a single transactional Postgres RPC (converge with the existing tb_ingest_* direct RPCs) so a Cloud Run timeout cannot leave a tenant half-written; add a post-ingest record-count consistency check.

Implement a per-run sync-outcome heartbeat POST from the connector to the backend, and build 'no heartbeat in N hours' + 'error rate > X per company' alerts (BetterStack alerting or a scheduled Cloud Run job) so client-side failures become operator-visible proactively.

Standardize on structured JSON logging (pino for Node, structlog/JSON-formatter for Python) with shared correlation fields (run_id, company, ingest_mode, app_version); stop deriving log level by regex and keep more than one rotated log file.

Fix the misleading client UI signals (StatusBar hardcoded internetOk=true and the cosmetic next-sync countdown) so the client's own first line of observability reflects reality during cloud-push failures.
toolingChoices: Sentry — @sentry/electron, @sentry/node, sentry_flutter (Dart), sentry-sdk (Python): unified crash + error aggregation with release/version tagging; DSN is write-only like the existing BetterStack token model the team already trusts.
BetterStack (Logtail/Better Uptime) — already integrated for Live Tail; extend it with Uptime monitors on the Cloud Run /readyz endpoints and alert policies on log patterns, avoiding a new vendor.
pino (Node, main + backend) and structlog or stdlib logging+python-json-logger (Python engine + parsing) — structured JSON logs with shared fields; pino-pretty for local dev.
GCP Cloud Monitoring uptime checks + alerting policies (Cloud Run is already on GCP) — health/latency/5xx alerts with no extra infra; route to email/Slack/PagerDuty.
tenacity (Python) for declarative retry/backoff-with-jitter in cloud_pusher.py, or a small hand-rolled loop if avoiding a dependency; for the backend, p-retry around PostgREST calls.
A single shared event schema (TypeScript type + Python TypedDict) for sync outcomes/heartbeats so Electron, backend, and Flutter emit comparable structured telemetry.
production.effort: Sentry rollout (all 4 surfaces): M. Real health checks + GCP uptime/alerting: S-M. Retry/backoff + idempotency in cloud_pusher: M. Transactional ingest RPC conversion: L (touches the 2992-line sync.ts and SQL RPCs, needs careful testing). Fix swallowed-success + escalate restore/schema errors: S. Heartbeat + alerting on sync failure: M. Structured logging standard: M (cross-cutting). UI signal fixes (StatusBar): S. Overall this dimension is a multi-week effort; the highest-ROI, lowest-effort first steps are Sentry, real /health checks + uptime alerting, and fixing the silent-success/swallowed-error paths."

production.currentState: The codebase ships working features but is in a pre-production hygiene state with no automated guardrails. There is ZERO lint/format/typecheck tooling across all four subsystems: no eslint/prettier config (none of .eslintrc*, eslint.config.*, .prettierrc* exist at root or in backend/), no Python ruff/black/mypy/flake8/pyproject (git ls-files shows none), and the only test script is backend's `"test": "echo \"Error: no test specified\" && exit 1"`. TypeScript strict mode IS enabled in all three tsconfigs (root, tsconfig.main.json, backend/tsconfig.json — backend even adds noUncheckedIndexedAccess + exactOptionalPropertyTypes), but it's undermined by pervasive `any`: 102 `any`/`as any`/Record<string,unknown> occurrences in backend/src and 26 in src/renderer+src/main, plus the entire IPC contract (electron.d.ts) typed as `any`. Python is fully untyped: 0 of 11 files in src/python import `typing`. Repo hygiene is poor: a narrow .gitignore (no `*.log`/`*.err`/`*.html`/`*.pdf` patterns), 22 stale compiler artifacts (.js/.d.ts/.map) committed INSIDE backend/src next to source, 63 tracked .md files (52 under md_files/), a 30-file orphan `frontend/` Vite app, committed log files, secrets (parsing/.env) sitting in git history, 19 untracked junk files at root one `git add .` from being committed, and no README or CONTRIBUTING anywhere. Four god-files dominate: backend/src/routes/sync.ts (2992 LOC), src/python/sync_main.py (1905 LOC, with in-flight "CHANGE 1-4" revert markers), src/python/cloud_pusher.py (933 LOC), src/python/tally_client.py (678 LOC).

findings.title: Compiler artifacts (.js/.d.ts/.map) committed inside backend/src next to TypeScript source
findings.evidence: git ls-files shows 22 tracked emitted files in backend/src: backend/src/routes/sync.js, sync.d.ts, sync.d.ts.map, sync.js.map and the same quartet for index, db/supabase, middleware/auth, routes/push-invoice, routes/push-voucher. backend/tsconfig.json now sets rootDir ./src + outDir ./dist, and the build script is bare `tsc`, so these are STALE duplicates from an earlier config (committed in 1f327d5/feeb928) that were never removed. No backend/.gitignore exists to keep them out.
findings.impact: Stale .js can be imported/run instead of fresh source (`npm start` runs node dist, but stray src/*.js confuse editors, grep, and ESM resolution under module:nodenext). Diffs are doubled and noisy; a developer editing sync.ts but accidentally running the committed sync.js silently runs old code. Pure rot that masks real changes in review.
findings.recommendation: git rm the 22 emitted files in backend/src, add a backend/.gitignore with `*.js`/`*.d.ts`/`*.map` under src (or better, dist/ + node_modules/), and confirm `tsc` emits only to dist/. Add a CI check that fails if compiled output appears under src/.

findings.title: No lint, format, or typecheck tooling or pre-commit hooks anywhere
findings.evidence: No eslint/prettier config at root or backend/ (probed .eslintrc*, eslint.config.*, .prettierrc*, .prettierignore — none). No Python linter/formatter config (no ruff.toml, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, .flake8, mypy.ini in git ls-files). No .husky/.pre-commit-config. backend test = `exit 1`. Tailwind+postcss+autoprefixer are in devDeps but unused (per digest).
findings.impact: Nothing mechanically prevents `any` proliferation, dead code, secret commits, or style drift. Every quality regression must be caught by human review, which is already failing (stale artifacts, dead code, committed history secrets all slipped through). For a paid client ship this is the single biggest process gap.
findings.recommendation: Add eslint (typescript-eslint) + prettier with a shared config consumed by root, backend, and frontend; add ruff (lint+format) for src/python and parsing/; wire `npm run lint`/`npm run typecheck` (tsc --noEmit) scripts and a husky/lint-staged or pre-commit hook running them on changed files. Drop tailwind/postcss/autoprefixer from devDeps since renderer uses 100% inline styles, or actually wire it.

findings.title: IPC type contract (electron.d.ts) is hand-maintained, already drifted, and entirely `any`-typed
findings.evidence: src/renderer/electron.d.ts declares the window.electronAPI surface with getConfig/saveSettings/addCompany etc. but OMITS getStartupSetting, setStartupSetting, openLogFile — all three exist in src/main/preload.ts (lines 40,41,44) and are called from Settings.tsx. Every method is typed `Promise<any>`/`(s:any)`. There is no generated bridge.
findings.impact: Runtime works but the type contract is a lie: any channel signature change (rename, arg shape) compiles clean and breaks only at runtime in front of the client. With strict mode on, this is the one place strictness is fully defeated.
findings.recommendation: Define a single shared IpcApi interface in src/main and have both preload.ts and the renderer consume it (import type), eliminating the hand-kept .d.ts. Type each channel's payload/return concretely. As an interim, add the 3 missing methods and replace `any` with real types so drift surfaces at compile time.

findings.title: Secrets committed to git history (parsing/.env) — not removable by deletion alone
findings.evidence: `git log --all -- parsing/.env` returns commits ae5872a, 51895e3, 434da8b. The file is no longer in the working tree (git ls-files shows none) but remains fully recoverable from history. Per the architecture digest it contained service_role Supabase key + RunPod key + Firebase private key.
findings.impact: Anyone with repo (or a fork/clone) access can `git show ae5872a:parsing/.env` and obtain full write access to the yynuu Supabase project and the Firebase project. Deleting the file does nothing; the credentials are exposed for the life of the history.
findings.recommendation: Rotate ALL credentials in that file immediately (treat as compromised), then scrub history with git-filter-repo/BFG and force-push (coordinate with collaborators). Add `*.env` already covered by .gitignore — verify parsing/ is covered. This overlaps the security dimension but is fundamentally a repo-hygiene failure.

findings.title: Narrow .gitignore lets 19 junk files at root sit one `git add .` from being committed
findings.evidence: Root .gitignore has no `*.log`/`*.err`/`*.out`/`*.html`/`*.pdf`/`*.txt` patterns (only node_modules, dist, release, *.pyc, _*.json etc.). git status shows 19 untracked: backend-3002.log/.err, backend-dev.{log,err,stderr.log,stdout.log}, backend-live.{log,err}, E2E_error_log.txt, multiple *_2026-06-17.html, TallyBridge_Walkthrough.pdf, SESSION_HANDOFF_2026-06-22.md, .tmp-ztugw-companies.js, command.txt, endpoints.txt, phase*_*.txt, run7_done.txt. Already-tracked precedent exists: backend/backend-dev.stderr.log, backend/backend-dev.stdout.log, parsing/server_test.log, parsing/server_test_err.log are committed.
findings.impact: Process artifacts and operational logs (some may contain tokens/URLs) keep leaking into the repo; the 4 already-committed log files prove the pattern. Bloats clone size and pollutes blame/diffs.
findings.recommendation: Add broad ignore rules: `*.log`, `*.err`, `*.out`, `*.tmp`, `*.tmp-*`, `.tmp-*`, `*.pdf`, `*.html` (or a /docs exception), plus `phase*_*.txt`, `*_done.txt`. git rm the 4 tracked log files. Move keep-worthy handoff docs into a single docs/ tree and ignore everything else at root.

findings.title: Four god-files concentrate the system's risk; sync_main.py carries in-flight revert markers
findings.evidence: wc -l: backend/src/routes/sync.ts=2992, src/python/sync_main.py=1905, src/python/cloud_pusher.py=933, src/python/tally_client.py=678, src/python/tally_pusher.py=531. sync.ts mixes auth, validation, ingest, push-queue, GCS proxy, dashboard reads, and an inventory-analytics engine. sync_main.py header carries explicit CHANGE 1/2/4 revert markers (per digest) — an experimental branch state, not settled design. cloud_pusher/tally_pusher import tally_client private internals (_post, _xml_escape, _fetch).
findings.impact: Every change to ingest, auth, or queue touches the same 3000-line file → high merge-conflict and regression surface, slow review, and the documented non-transactional ingest bugs live here. Reviewers cannot reason about a 2992-line file in front of a paying client.
findings.recommendation: Decompose by responsibility. Priority 1: split sync.ts into routes/sync (ingest), routes/push-queue, routes/reorder, services/ingest-tx, services/snapshot-restore, middleware reuse (collapse requireApiKey/requireClientApiKey). Priority 2: extract sync_main.py's voucher-window, parsing-ladder, and verify logic into modules and DELETE the CHANGE 1-4 reverted experimental code before ship (do not ship a half-reverted branch). Priority 3: give tally_client a public interface so cloud_pusher/tally_pusher stop importing `_`-prefixed internals.

findings.title: Dead Guided/non-Guided duplication and orphan components/dirs
findings.evidence: src/renderer/pages/Home.tsx and AddCompany.tsx are one-line re-exports of their *Guided siblings with the old buggy implementation left commented below (AddCompany's commented body references undefined setSelected/selected). Three CompanyCard variants exist (CompanyCard.tsx, CompanyCardGuided.tsx, CompanyCardStable.tsx) — only CompanyCardStable is active. A 30-file `frontend/` Vite app (frontend/package.json, eslint.config.js, index.html, public/) is committed but is not referenced by the Electron app's build (package.json build:renderer = `vite build` at root, files = dist/**). scanner/index.html + scanner/new/index.html are loose HTML.
findings.impact: New contributors cannot tell live from dead code; the commented originals contain real bugs presented as 'documentation'. The orphan frontend/ and scanner/ dirs add clone weight and confusion about which UI ships.
findings.recommendation: Delete the commented bodies in Home.tsx/AddCompany.tsx (git history preserves them); collapse the three CompanyCard variants to one. Determine if frontend/ and scanner/ are live products — if not, remove them from this repo or move to a clearly-labeled /experiments tree.

findings.title: No README, CONTRIBUTING, or runbook; duplicated bootstrap logic and dual config keys
findings.evidence: git ls-files shows no top-level README or CONTRIBUTING (frontend/ has its own README but the Electron root does not). Python command resolution is triplicated: sync-engine.ts:302/306, local-push-server.ts:114/220, push-queue-poller.ts:36/140 each rebuild the dev `py -3 -u sync_main.py` vs prod `process.resourcesPath/.../tallybridge-engine.exe` path independently. store.ts:34-37 keeps legacy backendUrl/apiKey AND controlPlaneUrl/controlPlaneApiKey, with resolve* helpers (store.ts:156) branching across both. Backend uses bespoke per-field validation with no schema validator (no zod/valibot/joi/yup in backend/package.json).
findings.impact: Onboarding a developer to a 4-runtime system (Electron TS + Python + Express + Flutter) with no entry doc is high-friction and error-prone. Triplicated spawn logic means a bundling/path change must be made in 3 places (easy to miss one → broken push or sync). Dual config keys double the branching surface and the chance of one path reading a stale value.
findings.recommendation: Add a root README (architecture + run/build/release commands — CLAUDE.md content is a good seed) and a CONTRIBUTING/runbook covering envs, secrets handling, and the release flow. Extract a shared resolvePythonCommand() helper used by all three main-process files. Pick controlPlane* as canonical, write a one-time migration, and delete the legacy keys + fallback branches. Adopt zod for /api/sync body validation.

recommendations: IMMEDIATE (pre-ship blocker): Rotate all credentials in parsing/.env (compromised via history commits ae5872a/51895e3/434da8b), then scrub history with BFG/git-filter-repo and force-push. Verify parsing/ is covered by .gitignore.

Add automated guardrails before client ship: eslint+prettier (shared config for root/backend/frontend), ruff for Python, `npm run typecheck` (tsc --noEmit) per package, and a husky/lint-staged or pre-commit hook running them on staged files. This is the highest-leverage process fix.

Clean the repo: git rm the 22 stale compiler artifacts in backend/src and the 4 committed *.log files; broaden .gitignore to cover *.log/*.err/*.out/*.tmp/*.tmp-*/*.html/*.pdf and add a backend/.gitignore. Then commit the 19 untracked junk files away (delete or ignore).

Delete dead code now (low risk, git preserves it): the commented bodies in Home.tsx/AddCompany.tsx, the two orphan CompanyCard variants, and decide the fate of orphan frontend/ (30 files) and scanner/ dirs.

Type the IPC boundary: define one shared IpcApi interface consumed by preload.ts and the renderer (drop the hand-kept electron.d.ts), adding the 3 missing channels and replacing `any` with concrete payload types.

Decompose god-files in priority order: (1) sync.ts 2992 LOC → ingest/queue/reorder/auth modules + a real transactional ingest service; (2) sync_main.py 1905 LOC → DELETE the reverted CHANGE 1-4 experimental code and split voucher/parse/verify modules; (3) give tally_client a public API so cloud_pusher/tally_pusher stop importing `_`-prefixed internals.

Add a root README + CONTRIBUTING/runbook (seed from CLAUDE.md), extract the triplicated resolvePythonCommand() helper, consolidate the legacy backendUrl/apiKey config keys onto controlPlane* via a migration, and introduce zod for backend request validation to retire 102 `any` sites incrementally.

Replace the backend's `test: exit 1` with a minimal vitest/pytest harness (even smoke tests on /api/sync validation and the parsing rule engine) so CI has something to gate on; without this, lint+typecheck are the only mechanical checks available.
toolingChoices: typescript-eslint (eslint v9 flat config) + Prettier — one shared config package consumed by root Electron, backend, and frontend; rationale: enforces no-explicit-any/no-unused-vars and kills style drift across the 3 TS surfaces with a single source of truth.

Ruff (lint + format, replaces black+flake8+isort in one fast tool) for src/python and parsing/, plus optional mypy in non-strict mode for new code; rationale: zero Python tooling exists today and 0/11 files use typing — Ruff is the lowest-friction way to add gradual quality without a heavy mypy migration.

Husky + lint-staged (Node side) and pre-commit framework (Python side), or a single pre-commit config covering both; rationale: mechanically blocks the exact failures already in the repo (secret commits, stale artifacts, junk files).
git-filter-repo (preferred over BFG for path-scoped scrubbing) to purge parsing/.env and committed *.log from history; rationale: deletion alone leaves secrets recoverable.

zod for backend request/payload validation; rationale: replaces 102 ad-hoc `any`/Record<string,unknown> normalizations in sync.ts with one declarative schema per endpoint and gives runtime safety the hand-rolled checks lack.

Vitest (backend/frontend) + pytest (python/parsing) to replace `test: exit 1`; rationale: gives CI an actual gate and lets the brittle parsing rule engine and non-transactional ingest get regression coverage where it matters most.
gitleaks or trufflehog as a CI/pre-commit secret scanner; rationale: the repo has already leaked a service_role + Firebase key — a scanner prevents recurrence after history scrub.
production.effort: Repo hygiene cleanup (gitignore + rm stale artifacts/logs + delete dead Guided code + secret rotation/history scrub): S-M, ~1-2 days, do FIRST. Tooling setup (eslint/prettier/ruff + pre-commit + typecheck scripts + secret scanner): M, ~2-3 days, parallelizable. IPC typing + dual-config consolidation + shared python-cmd helper: M, ~2-3 days. README/CONTRIBUTING/runbook: S, ~1 day. God-file decomposition is the long tail: sync.ts split=L (~1-2 weeks), sync_main.py de-revert+split=L (~1-2 weeks, must remove experimental CHANGE 1-4 before ship), cloud_pusher/tally_client public-API=M. Test harness bootstrap=M ongoing. Total to a defensible pre-ship hygiene baseline (everything except full god-file decomposition): roughly 1.5-2 weeks; full decomposition adds 3-4 weeks.
